newsitem.title: USA: Valencia harvest active in Florida citrus belt.
newsitem.headline: Valencia harvest active in Florida citrus belt.

text.p: Most groves are in very good condition in the Florida citrus belt this week, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.
There is an abundance of new growth in many groves. New crop fruit continues to make normal progress with harvest of Valencia oranges very active in all areas, according to FASS.
Caretakers are cutting cover crops that have grown tall and are competing with trees for soil nutrients. Spring herbicides are still being applied, FASS said.
FASS said an estimated 6,950,000 boxes of Valencia oranges were harvested in the week ended May 4, down from 7,534,000 in the prior week and compared with 6,616,000 during the week ended April 20.
